newsitem.title: INDIA: India LPG demand seen at 4.2 mln tonnes in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: India LPG demand seen at 4.2 mln tonnes in 96/97.

text.p: India's liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) consumption in financial 1996/97 (April-March) is expected to be 4.2 million tonnes, a senior company official said on Saturday.

"The LPG consumption during the current year is expected to be around 4.2 million tonnes," R.K. Narang, chairman of state-run Indian Oil Corp (IOC), told a petroleum technology conference in the Indian capital.
LPG consumption figures for 1995/96 were not available.
Narang said the annual demand for LPG is expected to rise to 9.5 million tonnes by 2001/02 and to 13.2 million tonnes by 2006/07.
"The vast potential demand for LPG in India would provide ample opportunity for growth of both public sector oil companies as well as private sector," Narang said.

He said that during the current year, two new "LPG import facilities", with annual capacity of 0.6 million tonnes each, were commisioned at Kandla in the western state of Gujarat and Mangalore in the southern state of Karnataka.
"This has enhanced the annual LPG import capacity of public sector companies from 0.7 million tonnes to 1.9 million," Narang said.
